newsitem.title: USA: ONBANCorp files suit vs shareholder.
newsitem.headline: ONBANCorp files suit vs shareholder.

text.p: ONBANCorp Inc said on Friday that it has commenced litigation against Seymour Holtzman, the bank's largest individual shareholder.

ONBANCorp's complaint, filed in federal district court in Syracuse, alleges that Holtzman has violated the federal proxy rules by publicly disseminating materially false and misleading information about ONBANCorp and its directors.
Attempts to reach Holtzman were unsuccessful.

Robert J. Bennett, ONBANCorp's chairman and chief executive officer, said, "Our board of directors believes quite strongly that Seymour Holtzman has misled the marketplace and ONBANCorp's stockholders in order to further his own personal agenda."
A statement issued by the company accused Holtzman of trying to agitate for the quick sale of the company.
Earlier this month, Holtzman proposed the merger or sale of the bank to a stronger financial institution.
At the time, Holtzman said ONBANCorp "simply has not earned the right to remain public," citing what he called the "dismal performance" of the bank's stock.
Holtzman's lawyer, Charles Garcia of the Boca Raton firm of Garcia & Cope, called the allegations "false, frivolous and a waste of corporate assets."

Garcia said Holtzman will hold management of the company personally responsible for wasting money on "this bid to preserve their jobs and to hide from shareholders their dismal performance over the last three years."

"If they want a fight Mr. Holtzman will give it to them, no problem," Garcia said. "We have 20 days to respond and respond we will, probably through a counter law suit and we will take a close look at going after the managers of this company personally for gross mismanagement."
Holtzman owns about 250,000 shares of ONBANCorp, or about two percent of the total number of shares, Garcia said.
Garcia said the price of the stock three years ago was about 41-1/4. The stock was at 35-1/4 in late afternoon trading Friday.
The Keefe, Bruyette & Wood 50-Bank Index during the same period increased 70 percent, Garcia said.
